speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: The schoolhouse door is bolted with the great staple on a Sunday, Edmund. You can walk past it without your Latin and the master cannot call you in.

speaker: edmund_shakespeare
text: He can call me in tomorrow morning if I drop a word of the syntax. Keep off the mounting-block, or Grandmother will say we are climbing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That oak door looked twice as wide when I was twelve and coming down Chapel Street with cold fingers.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Did you ever know the lesson before the bell stopped, Father, or did you invent it on the stair?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I knew the Latin when Ovid had a story in it, Susanna, and the master knew the birch when he had not.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Look at the chapel wall, Edmund. It is white, and the school is shut above it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Step out past the school stair. We have Old Town still between us and the porch.
